The World is Changing: AI For Creativity

By Jeffrey Katzenberg

A few months ago, I sat in my office in Silicon Valley and watched as a tech founder showed me something extraordinary. On the screen was a fully realized, beautifully lit, well-composed animated scene. It was stunning and it made me feel exactly what I felt in 1986 watching Luxo Jr. That was the first time I watched a computer-animated 3D character take a breath and seem, against all reason, to have life. It left me in awe.

Later that day, I received a text from an artist I've known for thirty years, 350 miles to the south, in the city where I spent most of my career. After seeing a similar video, she texted: "Is this the end of us?" My answer was, "Certainly not.”

​
Just dropped a research note on who is actually buying tokenised assets.
Here’s your TL;DR ↓
– Arrakis looked at 71,697 buyers and $91.3B in gross onchain acquisitions across 10 tokenised dollar-yield products.
– The surprise isn't demand size — it's who's behind it: mostly crypto-native institutions, not traditional TradFi allocators.
– Wallets with $1M+ controlled about 93% of capital while making up only 4% of buyers.
– Of the identifiable $12.4B in demand, about 66% came from DAO and protocol treasuries.
– Most purchases still happen through primary subscription; for most products, DEX entry was only 0%–6%.
– RWA marketing looks less like retail growth and more like institutional B2B sales: awareness, diligence, compliance, then allocation.
– The buyer set is narrow, but the decision process is wide — hidden stakeholders inside funds, exchanges and DAOs still need research, proof and clean risk framing.
– The practical implication: issuers need to market to onchain institutions, especially across EMEA and APAC hours, and build trust before anyone hits subscribe.
Read the full story here:
Marketing RWAs: who is actually buying tokenised assets?
